prompt: A wooden crate of mass 50 kg rests on a rough horizontal floor. The maximum limiting static friction between the crate and the floor is 160 N. A horizontal pushing force of 95 N is applied to the crate. State the magnitude of the frictional force acting on the crate and state whether the crate moves.

mark_scheme.criterion: The crate does not move (remains stationary) because the applied force does not exceed the maximum limiting static friction.

hints: Compare the applied force (95 N) with the limiting static friction (160 N).
Static friction self-adjusts to prevent motion.
solution: Frictional force is 95 N. The crate does not move because the applied force is less than the maximum limiting static friction (95 N < 160 N).
teacher_walkthrough: Since 95 N < 160 N, the crate does not budge (B1).
Static friction balances the applied force exactly to keep resultant force zero: F_friction = 95 N (B1).
A common pitfall is writing 160 N for the frictional force.
